posts.cooked:
While I'm a bit disappointed at apparently not getting Biomancer's episode any time soon, I remember Christopher saying he wanted to do something really special for the 40th episode, so I'm not at all surprised they went for Guise's episode. Plus it makes Powerhound happy!

Although the Fanatic and Apostate and Wager Master episodes are probably going to be outright crazy in their own right. Whoo boy. Actually, this is pretty much the entire month of "let's explain all the really really crazy weird characters that are going to have weird existential cosmic relevance".

Speaking of Biomancer, though, it was interesting to find out a bit more about what really happened with Con, and I feel like I can now go back to picturing Chrono and Con as Sam and Al again. Though now I'm even more interested in just what the heck Biomancer's ultimate motivations are for all these shenangians.

Finding out my precious psychic child apparently got to hold an entire important hero party makes me not mind waiting until the OblivAeon ep. :D Also it seems the Tactics timeline continues to suck a whole bunch, hands up everyone who's surprised...

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
When Biomancer didn't immediately follow the Scholar, I felt for sure they were saving him for the Halloween episode.  But no, we get Wager Master--who, to be fair, is probably the most terrifying villain of all.

CON is turning out to be much more interesting that we suspected.  Now we know that Biomancer is responsible for his turning "evil" temporarily.  We know that CON deliberately aligned the time badge to absorb the energy of Chrono's successful bounties, effectively forcing him to obey as instructed or be stuck.  And we also know that CON's ability to move Chrono within his own timestream is a result of OblivAeon somehow.  I hope we get all of this explained at some point.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
I had no idea/forgot this episode was coming, so I ended up taking an impromptu and unplanned walk this evening! Thanks for helping keep me in shape, Christopher and Adam!

Gotta say, I love the use of Miss Info's theme and the victory music instead of the usual musical cues. :D Those help this new Editor's Note thing stand apart from regular episodes. And on that note, definitely less exciting than an episode, but still fascinating and worth listening to.

If nothing else, I'm most pleased that they talked about their actual creation process some. That seems to be the one aspect of Sentinels Comics that isn't touched on often, and I can understand why, but seeing how Writhe started as basically "this shadow villain Tachyon punched once" is a great peek under the curtain.

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
I always feel a bit sad when Adam complains about his old art.

He has definitely gotten better in quality, but his composition skills and the personality of his art has always been top-notch. And for me those are what I look for most in artwork; there's far too much art which is pretty from a technical standpoint but is really flat and dull from an actual composition standpoint.

(I of course won't say no to having both technical quality AND good composition, but if I had to pick which one I was willing to give on...)

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked: Jeysie you nailed it.  I'll take a good story poorly written on beautifully crafted drivel any day.  And I'll take Adams old art over a lot of technically better art thwt isn't engaging.  I know people who are the opposite though, and yes, both is always better.

posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
But, at the same time, you are always you're own harshest critic and I'm certain Adam is not wrong on any of his critics of his work. He just sees all the flaws every time he looks at his work instead of all the good things he did as well.

 

Honestly, I think Christopher kind of gets to cheat in this department as compared to Adam. As the "Story guy" to a story that is largely nebulous and ill-defined at times (What exactly did Judge Mental say that pushed IDealist over the edge instead of sealing the break-up of the Sentinels?) almost all the minor details that make or break the type of crtique that Adam is applying to his art is invisible or non-existent.

 

I'm sure if this were an actual comic book company and we had pages of dialogue to go through, Christopher would be just as likely to bemoan how badly he did five years or more ago as Adam is. Adam just got stuck with the job that required more immediate detailing that can't be easily redone.

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
I do admit I think there are some heroes with dialogue that sounds odd/stilted on their flavor text (Nightmist and Argent being the two worst sufferers), but I haven't been disappointed with what actual comics we've gotten. (Part of why I'm excited at getting eventual Prime Wardens scenario comics in Tactics.)

But there's a different mindset between appreciating how far you've come and genuinely hating the previous stuff you did when it's not actually that bad. Admittedly Adam has the unenviable position as an artist where his early art is a widespread publication rather than tucked safely away in personal or limited release projects and sketchbooks.

It's just I always see people talking about Adam hating his old art, and I sometimes wonder about Christopher's side of that equation.

 

Frankly, I've rarely met an artist who liked his current art, let alone one who didn't say he hated his old stuff. It feels natural to me, so I just decided to vent some thoughts about it. I don't disagree that I also like Adam's old art, and there is a point where self-criticism becomes more destructive than useful, but we're just not in a position for that call I think.
